title: Momentum is building for better data in the Caribbean, but more work lies ahead
gist: World Bank Statistical Performance Indicator scores for eight Caribbean upper-middle/high-income countries rose from 42.8 in 2016 to 60.1 in 2024, still below the UMIC average of 68.9. Gains come from data access and infrastructure, while core data collection and data use barely moved.

insights.claim: The average Statistical Performance Indicators score for eight upper-middle and high-income Caribbean countries rose from 42.8 in 2016 to 60.1 in 2024, a gain of 17.26 points.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Official Caribbean macro and social data are becoming more available and reliable.

insights.claim: Caribbean countries still underperform income peers: the 2024 average SPI for upper middle-income countries was 68.9, with Small Island Developing State status (small, open economies with high per-capita costs of producing statistics) a likely partial reason.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Residual data-quality discounts persist for Caribbean sovereigns relative to peers.

insights.claim: Haiti's SPI score rose only from 36.2 in 2016 to 38.7 in 2024, far below the lower middle-income average of 63, reflecting recurrent shocks and persistent security challenges.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Haiti remains close to a data blackout, complicating any risk or humanitarian assessment.

insights.claim: Data Services improved most, from 12.4 in 2016 to 63.8 in 2024, as more countries publish open machine-readable data and Jamaica, Belize and Suriname improved access to granular datasets.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Easier access to microdata improves outside analysis of these economies.
insights.locator: Caribbean countries have made data more accessible

insights.claim: Data Infrastructure rose from 35.6 in 2016 to 53.8 in 2024, driven by stronger statistics legislation and wider adoption of international standards.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Legal and institutional foundations are in place to support further statistical improvement.
insights.locator: Caribbean countries have made data more accessible

insights.claim: SDG reporting coverage expanded most for economic, social and institutional statistics between 2016 and 2024, while environmental statistics reporting (SDGs 13 and 15) declined overall.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Climate-exposed Caribbean states are reporting less environmental data, a gap for climate risk analysis.

insights.claim: The Data Sources pillar is the Caribbean's lowest-scoring, improving only from 47.4 in 2016 to 50.3 in 2024, as countries became less likely to have up-to-date population and housing censuses, agricultural censuses and health and demographic surveys.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Stale censuses undermine denominators for per-capita and poverty statistics across the region.
insights.locator: More work is needed to collect new data

insights.claim: Data Use scored 68.8 in 2016 and 69.6 in 2024, with some countries improving and others declining, though several small countries score strongly, showing small size is not a barrier to using data in policy.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Small size does not preclude good statistical practice, so weak scores reflect choices and resources.
insights.locator: The score for Data Use increased

insights.claim: Accessible data portals and modern statistics laws will not be enough if underlying data are not being collected, so slow progress on Data Sources and Data Use threatens to hold systems back.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Portal-level improvements may overstate the true quality of regional statistics.
insights.locator: More work is needed to collect new data

insights.claim: Identifying a common minimum set of data, standards and practices across Caribbean small island states could let countries exploit economies of scale with support from regional bodies and development partners.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Watch for pooled regional statistical initiatives as the delivery model.

insights.claim: The 2030 Population and Housing Census round is an opportunity to align planning, methods, technical assistance and funding, building on the October 2025 Caribbean Data Day organized by the World Bank and CARICOM.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Census funding and coordination are the near-term milestone for regional data quality.
insights.locator: The upcoming 2030 Population and Housing Census round

insights.claim: Regional initiatives such as the OECS Data for Decision Making Project and Poverty and Equity Assessments already use available data to inform national policy priorities.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Existing programs give a base for the proposed coordinated push.
